main_issue: The Axis case directly supports an attacker-controlled JNDI name reaching lookup through an incomplete scheme denylist, but the DataEase case provides only patch-backed retrieval provenance and no source, sink, guard, or exploit-path evidence tying it to JNDI or remote lookup.
evidence_notes: CVE-2023-51441: environment[jndiName] is filtered by an incomplete protocol denylist and then passed to InitialContext.lookup(name); omitted IIOP/CORBANAME schemes support the stated untrusted-JNDI-target mechanism.

CVE-2025-58045: supplied evidence identifies Impala.getJdbc and Db2.getJdbc as review-entry spans, but does not establish attacker control, JDBC URL construction, remote connection behavior, or any JNDI/naming-context sink.

The cluster summary mixes JDBC parameter injection, JNDI scheme injection, and SQL string concatenation. These are distinct mechanisms and cannot serve as supporting evidence for this JNDI-focused guideline without per-case traces.
